100.definition: When two variables are compared in a system.
100.design: Variable as part of a system.
100.name: variable

101.definition: A nominal variable has values of equal importance that cannot be ranked in any particular order (non-ordinal), e.g., species of pests, colors. The values of these variables are usually indicated by words, ideally using controlled lists.
101.name: nominal

102.definition: An ordinal variable has values corresponding to a list of concepts that can be put in a certain order but are not measured. They are generally qualitative, and the classes can therefore only be ordered in relation to each other. Dates are also ordinal values.
102.design: Generalize the property and put the specialization into the OoI (single). It requires a matrix.
102.name: ordinal

103.definition: A binary or boolean property allows exactly two values: true/false, good/bad. Quality flags are boolean.
103.design: OoI with single. A constraint of type 'threshold' should be added to explain when the quality flag holds. Sometimes, however, the object of interest is a whole variable (property plus object of interest).
103.name: boolean

104.definition: Assigns to an entity a non-negative integer equal to the number of distinct related entities satisfying a declared relation and scope.
104.name: count

105.definition: A unitless property with integer values (excluding counts) that are physically enforced. They can be constants or variable numbers.
105.design: Use single entity in the object of interest.
105.name: discrete

106.definition: Length of a discrete object. Length is a fundamental property. Examples are width, depth, height, circumference.
106.name: length

107.definition: Length in relation to another object. Length is a fundamental property. Examples are width, depth, height, circumference.
107.design: OoI with single. Length requires a reference point given by a constraint (reference).
107.name: length ref

109.definition: Fundamental properties are physical quantities that are conventionally accepted as functionally independent of all others, excluding lengths. These are thermodynamic temperature, time, mass, amount of substance, luminous intensity, electric current.
109.name: fundamental

110.definition: A fraction is a ratio comparing a part to the whole where the quantities (quantitative property) are of the same kind.
110.name: fraction

111.definition: Cover expresses the fraction of a total reference area that is occupied by the Object of Interest.
111.design: Asymmetric system (numerator/denominator) at the object of interest slot. The portion is represented by the numerator, the total reference area by the denominator.
111.name: property (cover)

112.definition: A unitless ratio comparing two geometric properties of the same kind to describe the intrinsic, static shape of a single object (e.g., Aspect Ratio).
112.design: Use single entity in the object of interest.
112.name: geometric ratio

113.definition: A quantity that describes physical relationships or the physical state of a system without an associated physical unit.
113.design: Use single entity in the object of interest.
113.name: dimensionless physical ratio

114.definition: A derived property without ratio-transformation from fundamental quantities like volume or area.
114.name: ratioless derived

115.definition: A relative quantity whose value is expressed relative to an explicit baseline, reference standard, or nominal state, rather than as an explicit physical ratio of two variable entities.
115.name: normalized

116.definition: An angle measured against a local/arbitrary reference frame (e.g., the angle between two intersecting pipes, or the joint angle of a knee).
116.name: angle

117.definition: A spatial or angular measurement indicating the orientation, heading, or trajectory of an entity relative to a specified reference frame (vector).
117.design: OoI with two parts. One part must be the reference vector.
117.name: direction

118.definition: A temporal property measuring the number of discrete, countable events or occurrences that take place within a specified period of time.
118.name: event rate

119.definition: The scalar rate at which an object covers distance over time, representing the magnitude of motion regardless of direction.
119.name: speed

120.definition: Vector property that measures the rate of change of an object's position with respect to time, combining both speed (magnitude) and direction.
120.design: OoI with single. Requires a constraint of type direction or reference
120.name: velocity

121.definition: Count of individual entities per mass of a medium.
121.name: massic number density

122.definition: Mole per mass including molality (denominator is mass of the solvent component) and substance content (denominator is mass of the total mixture).
122.design: Use asymmetric system in the object of interest.
122.name: massic amount of substance

123.definition: Quantity per length, example is linear mass density.
123.name: lineic density

124.design: Property with constraint of type normalization. OoI single.
124.name: normalized count

125.design: OoI with ratio and optional matrix patterns.
125.name: volumic number density

126.definition: A property that is inherent to the substance's chemical composition and molecular structure, like plasticity, volumic density, absorbance.
126.name: intrinsic

127.design: OoI with ratio and optional matrix patterns.
127.name: areal density

128.definition: Concentration describes how much of one substance (the solute) is present in another substance (the solvent) as a volume. Examples are mass and amount of substance concentration.
128.design: Requires an ObjectOfInterest to be an asymmetric system of type ratio with numerator and denominator.
128.name: concentration

129.definition: A ratio rate with an energy flow represented in a simplified way.
129.design: OoI with single and Matrix with an optional natural container. Often the property is domain-specific labelled such as actinic flux.
129.name: flux simplified

130.definition: A ratio rate with a material flow from a source to a target while the denominator is represented by an area.
130.design: OoI with single and Matrix with flow patterns.
130.name: flux simple

131.definition: A ratio rate with a material flow from a source to a target. Complex representation is needed when there needs to be a constraint on the denominator.
131.design: OoI with ratio and Matrix with flow patterns.
131.name: flux complex

132.definition: An index acts as a proxy property that normalizes data against a specific base point or reference value to provide relative context rather than absolute measurement. While it sometimes aggregates multiple variables into a single score, its primary function is to make diverse data sets comparable over time or across different subjects.
132.design: Index must be specified (e.g. body mass index). OoI is a single entity.
132.name: index

133.definition: Length between two objects, where one of the two is constraint.
133.name: distance ref

134.definition: Energy per amount of substance (molar energy).
134.name: energy per mole

135.definition: Radioactivity content of chemical substance per mass.
135.name: massic activity

136.definition: A statistical measure becomes a statistical property when it changes the dimension of the property of the measurement like variance and confidence interval.
136.name: statistical property

137.design: Use single entity in the object of interest.
137.name: instant

138.definition: Properties resulting in quantitative numbers that represent ordered points along a continuous scale with equal, measurable distances between adjacent units, but without a true absolute zero point.
138.design: Use single entity in the object of interest.
138.name: interval

139.definition: Probability is a numerical measure of how likely a specific event is to occur. It quantifies chance or uncertainty on a scale strictly bounded between 0 and 1 (or 0% and 100%).
139.design: Use single entity in the object of interest.
139.name: probability

140.definition: A property that acts as an atomic (scalar) concept, derived from fundamental physical dimensions. Examples are acceleration and speed.
140.name: atomic derived property

141.definition: The rate at which an object's velocity changes with respect to time.
141.name: acceleration

142.design: Requires an ObjectOfInterest to be an asymmetric system of type ratio with numerator and denominator.
142.name: areic amount of substance

200.definition: A constraint that specifies a single principle, standard, or rule used to make a judgment or decision.
200.design: Apply the constraint on constrained component
200.name: criterion

201.definition: A constraint that specifies the distance in the line of advance of a wave from any one point to the next point of corresponding phase.
201.design: Apply the constraint on constrained component
201.name: wavelength

202.definition: A constraint that specifies an order relation that formalizes the notion of sorting elements.
202.design: Apply the constraint on constrained component
202.name: order

203.definition: A constraint that specifies the average kinetic energy of the particles (atoms or molecules) in a substance, determining how hot or cold it is.
203.design: Apply the constraint on constrained component
203.name: temperature

204.definition: A constraint that specifies the surrounding area, neighborhood, or general proximity near a specific place or landmark.
204.design: Apply the constraint on constrained component
204.name: vicinity

205.definition: A constraint defined as an evaluation, assessment, or classification of something against a standardized scale or set of criteria.
205.design: Apply the constraint on constrained component
205.name: rating

206.definition: A constraint defined as the length of a straight line through the center of an object or space.
206.design: Apply the constraint on constrained component
206.name: diameter

207.definition: A constraint defined as a systematic arrangement in groups or categories according to established criteria.
207.design: Apply the constraint on constrained component
207.name: classification

208.definition: A constraint defined as an intrinsic physical property of a material that measures how strongly it opposes or resists the flow of electric current.
208.design: Apply the constraint on constrained component
208.name: resistivity

209.definition: A constraint defined refers to the visible, structural, or material state of an object or substance, describing its physical appearance, state of matter, or spatial shape.
209.design: Apply the constraint on constrained component
209.name: physical form

33.definition: A single, distinguishable "object" in the universe, for which a property is measured.
33.design: Object of interest with a single entity.
33.name: single

34.definition: A system with two parts having the same role in the description.
34.design: Symmetric system in the object of interest
34.name: two equal

35.definition: The variable compares two quantities by division and tells you how much of one thing there is relative to another.
35.design: object of interest (asymmetric System, with numerator and denominator description roles)
35.name: ratio

36.definition: A system of entities where the source is the reference of the target.
36.design: object of interest (asymmetric system, with source and target description roles)
36.name: reference

37.definition: An object, that is semantically complex and overloaded
37.design: Simple object of interest, constrained and potentially requires a matrix to be deconvoluted.
37.name: convoluted

38.definition: When there is a property of the property of interest
38.design: the second property becomes the role of the object of interest, requires in addition the matrix. Depending on the property type the object of interest is either a system or a single entity.
38.name: property

39.definition: When there is a property of a variable.
39.design: the variable gets the role of the object of interest
39.name: variable

40.definition: The matrix must be of a different material than the object of interest. If the material is the same, the description component has a context object role.
40.name: embedding material

41.definition: A matrix is required when the object of interest is contained in a natural body.
41.name: natural container

42.definition: A matrix is required when the object of interest is contained in an artificial vessel.
42.name: artificial container

43.definition: A phenomenon in which the object is involved.
43.design: The phenomena must be repesented with a simple matrix.
43.name: natural process

44.definition: Is an area that acts as reference like a study area.
44.name: reference area

45.definition: Flow of material from one source to a target.
45.design: A matrix as asymmetric system is required for a flux property. The components associated with to the system are source and target, via the respective properties hasSource and hasTarget.
45.name: flow

50.definition: Can be a natural or artificial environment, which is not the matrix itself. Sometimes it is required to distinguish it from another environment.
50.name: environment

60.definition: A constraint defined as the systematic process of facilitating learning, acquiring knowledge, skills, values, beliefs, and habits through instruction, training, research, or discussion.
60.design: Apply the constraint on constrained component
60.name: education

61.definition: A constraint defined as a significant connection, association, or involvement between two or more people, groups, or entities, characterized by mutual interaction, influence, or relevance.
61.design: Apply the constraint on constrained component
61.name: relationship

62.definition: A constraint that specifies an entity, either human, artificial, biological, or organizational, that senses its environment and acts upon it autonomously to achieve a specific goal or purpose.
62.design: Apply the constraint on constrained component
62.name: agent

64.definition: provides a material type information about the constrained component
64.name: material type

66.definition: provides the sampling frequency that applies for the constrained component
66.name: sampling frequency

67.definition: provides a location-specific information about the constrained component
67.name: location

68.definition: provides a reference point or information for the constrained component
68.name: reference

69.definition: constraints the component specifying in which layer the variable is measured
69.name: layer

70.definition: a contextual circumstance or environmental feature that limits or qualifies the constrained component
70.name: condition

72.definition: indicates the cause or originating factor that explains why the constrained component occurs or holds
72.name: cause

73.definition: provides specific information enabling better interpretation of the constrained component
73.name: constraint (interpretation)

74.definition: indicates the spatial coverage within which the constrained component applies
74.name: spatial extent

75.definition: indicates the temporal coverage within which the constrained component applies
75.name: temporal extent

76.definition: indicates the physical, chemical or qualitative condition, including phases, of the constrained component
76.name: state

77.definition: indicates the role a person might have in the context of the variable
77.design: constraint on entity, entity must be a human
77.name: role

78.definition: provides time-specific information about the constrained component
78.name: time

79.definition: specifies the source, provenance, or starting point of the constrained component
79.name: source

80.definition: is the arrangement of individual entities or measurements across a specific geographic area or 3D space
80.design: constraint on statistical modifier or entity
80.name: spatial distribution

81.definition: provides the range of allowed values
81.name: range

82.definition: defines the value limit that triggers a quality flag, indicating whether the measurement satisfies the threshold criterion.
82.name: threshold

83.definition: defines how often a final data point is reported
83.name: reporting frequency

84.definition: specifies the degree of quality or purity of a substance or generally of the component
84.name: purity

87.definition: specifies the quantity in which the entity occurs
87.name: quantity

88.definition: refers to the distinct physiological, kinematic, or mechanical mode of self-propelled movement exhibited by an organism.
88.name: locomotion state

90.definition: refers to a process that occurs when measuring the property
90.name: process

91.definition: Identifies a specific occurrence, that bounds or triggers the observation, serving as a contextual anchor when explicit calendar time or duration is unknown or non-applicable.
91.design: Apply the constraint on the constrained component.
91.name: event

92.definition: Specifies the reference quantity to which a measurement is rescaled.
92.design: Apply the constraint on the denominator of the asymmetric system.
92.name: normalization

94.definition: A constraint that specifies a structural, anatomical, or biological sub-component (e.g., leaf, liver, root, surface layer) of an entity.
94.design: Apply the constraint on constrained component
94.name: part

95.definition: A constraint that restricts the human subject or population to a defined age interval, specific age value, or life stage.
95.design: Apply the constraint on constrained component
95.name: age

96.definition: A constraint that specifies the spatial orientation, vector heading, or flow orientation (e.g., downward, northward, incoming, outward) of the observed phenomenon relative to a spatial coordinate system, physical boundary, or reference feature. When the direction is defined relative to an absolute, globally understood coordinate system, a reference constraint is redundant and unnecessary.
96.name: direction

97.definition: A constraint that specifies an area of land or space that shares unifying characteristics, setting it apart from surrounding areas.
97.design: Apply the constraint on constrained component
97.name: region

98.definition: A constraint defined as a series of systematic, ordered actions or steps taken to achieve a specific end or result.
98.design: Apply the constraint on constrained component
98.name: process

99.definition: A constraint defined as a linguistic mechanism, point of origin, or benchmark used to locate events, actions, or states in time relative to another point in time.
99.design: Apply the constraint on constrained component
99.name: temporal reference
